newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND FALL TO ZIMBABWE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND FALL TO ZIMBABWE AGAIN.

text.p: England failed to improve their dismal record against Zimbabwe on Sunday as they slumped to a two-wicket defeat in the first one-day international at Queen's Club.

England's bowlers did their best to make up for a shocking batting display by reducing the hosts to 107 for seven, but Zimbabwe skipper Alistair Campbell saw his side past England's paltry total of 152 with 6.1 overs to spare.
Zimbabwe have only won eight of their 63 one-day internationals, but remarkably three of those victories have now come at the expense of England.
Put into bat on a benign wicket England made a confident start thanks to Alec Stewart, but when he edged a Heath Streak delivery to wicketkeeper Andy Flower the innings went into terminal decline.
Skipper Mike Atherton took 25 balls to get off the mark and then slogged a catch to mid on when he had done the hard work in making 23 from 77 balls.
Thereafter it was left to Nasser Hussain to hold the innings together. The Essex man played sensibly to score 49 not out off 87 balls, but could do nothing about the carnage at the other end.

The last six wickets fell for 28 runs and England were guilty of not using all their overs, being bowled out in the 46th. The seam of John Rennie snared three wickets for 27 runs, while the more respectable pace of Heath Streak accountd for three more for 30.

Debutant paceman Chris Silverwood inspired the rest of England's attack when he took a wicket in his first over. Darren Gough chipped in with the wickets of Dave Houghton and Craig Evans and Alan Mullally threw the game into the melting pot with two wckets in two balls.

But from 106 for seven, the left-handed Campbell hauled Zimbabwe back into the game with a mature knock of 32 not out which won him the man of the match award. He hit the winning runs down to long leg off Ronnie Irani to give his team a famous victory.
Zimbabwe now lead the three-match series 1-0, with the final two matches scheduled to follow the test series which begins here on Wednesday.
